title: The Last Cigar of Edmund Vale
intro: Rain hammers Vale Manor. Edmund Vale, shipping magnate, lies dead in his study with a bronze paperweight beside his head. The household swears it was a quiet evening. One of them is lying. Find the killer, then accuse.

locations.name: Foyer
locations.description: A drafty hall of black-and-white tile and dripping umbrellas. Doors lead to the study, the library and the kitchen.

locations.name: Study
locations.description: Leather, ink and the copper smell of blood. Vale's body has been covered with a coat.

locations.name: Library
locations.description: Floor-to-ceiling shelves and a chessboard with the game left half finished.

locations.name: Kitchen
locations.description: Copper pots and a cold stove. The window overlooks the drive, and a back door opens onto the garden.

locations.name: Garden
locations.description: Wet roses and a gravel path under the study window. The rain has not washed everything away.

people.name: Victor Crane
people.description: Vale's business partner. Silver hair, a flawless suit, and a smile that does not move his eyes.

talk.text: Dreadful business. I left at nine sharp and went straight to my club. I never set foot in the study after dinner.
Very well, my car was still on the drive. It would not start. That proves nothing about the study.

people.name: Dr. Mara Quill
people.description: The family physician, hands folded, eyes tired. She was a guest for the night.

talk.text: Julian and I played chess from nine until well past ten. He never left the board, I would stake my licence on it.

people.name: Julian Vale
people.description: The dead man's nephew. Rumpled, restless, and clearly in need of a drink.

talk.text: Yes, Uncle and I fought over my debts this evening. That does not make me a murderer.
Those prints under the window are mine. I went out to sulk at seven. After nine I was with Dr. Quill.
A cigar in Uncle's study? Those are Crane's. He lights Havana Reservas everywhere and it drove Uncle mad.

people.name: Mrs. Pell
people.description: The housekeeper. Sturdy, sharp-eyed, and unimpressed by gentlemen.

talk.text: Around eight I heard raised voices in the study. Master Julian, shouting about money.
A cigar? Mr. Vale never touched tobacco. Doctor's orders, and he hated the smell in his study.
When I locked the back door at ten, Mr. Crane's black Daimler was still on the drive. He says he left at nine. I say he did not.

items.name: stopped clock
items.description: The mantel clock lies smashed on the hearth, its hands frozen at twenty to ten.

items.name: cigar stub
items.description: A fresh stub in the ashtray, still wearing a gold Havana Reserva band.

items.name: torn IOU
items.description: A scrap of paper in Julian's hand, promising Vale a very large sum, torn in half.

items.name: muddy footprints
items.description: A man's shoe prints in the flowerbed, leading to the study window and back.

clues.text: The study clock was smashed and stopped at 9:40, so Vale died at twenty to ten.
A fresh Havana Reserva cigar stub was left in the ashtray of the study.
Vale never smoked; he forbade tobacco in his study.
Victor Crane habitually smokes Havana Reserva cigars.
Crane claims he left at nine sharp and never entered the study after dinner.
Crane's car was still on the drive at ten, an hour after he claimed to have left.
Julian signed an IOU for a large sum to his uncle, which was torn in half.
Julian was heard shouting at Vale about money around eight o'clock.
A man's muddy footprints lead to and from the study window.

solution.explanation: Vale died at 9:40 (c_clock). A cigar stub lay in the study (c_cigar), but Vale never smoked (c_nosmoke), and it was Crane's brand (c_brand). Crane swore he left at nine and never returned to the study (c_claim), yet his car was still on the drive at ten (c_car). Julian had motive (debt, quarrel, footprints) but was playing chess with Dr. Quill at 9:40, so only Crane fits.
